forces.title: RBI's expanded Upper Layer NBFC regulations increase oversight
forces.description: The RBI's draft amendments to the Scale-Based Regulation (SBR) for NBFCs will significantly expand the scope of the Upper Layer, bringing approximately 70% of total NBFC assets under stricter supervision by September 2025. This includes minimum CET I capital of 9%, compulsory stock exchange listing within three years, and enhanced disclosures. While strengthening financial stability, these measures will increase compliance costs and require improved governance, impacting operational models and capital planning for affected NBFCs.

forces.title: Gold loans maintain robust triple-digit growth fueled by high prices
forces.description: Advances to individuals against gold surged by 123.1% year-on-year in March 2026, accelerating from 121.1% in the previous year, with projected growth of 35% in FY26. This significant growth is attributed to elevated gold prices, which inflate the value of gold-backed loans, and the reclassification of agri-gold loans into the retail segment due to revised eligibility limits. This trend provides a substantial boost to NBFCs specializing in gold loans.

forces.title: Bank lending to NBFCs sees strong traction, driving NBFC funding
forces.description: Bank lending to Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) experienced significant traction in March 2026, with outstanding credit reaching Rs 20.65 lakh crore, representing 9.7% of total bank credit. This marked a substantial year-on-year growth of 26.3%, over four times the rate recorded a year ago. This robust momentum indicates NBFCs are increasingly shifting towards bank funding as an alternative to more expensive market borrowings, thereby strengthening their liquidity and operational capacity.

forces.title: Rising delinquencies in MFI and small-ticket unsecured segments
forces.description: The Microfinance Institutions (MFI) category experienced a significant rise in Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) by 74 basis points alongside a contraction in its loan book in H1 FY26. Similarly, MSME lending, especially for lower ticket sizes, has seen higher delinquencies recently, with credit costs expected to inch up to 1.7% in FY26 from 1.5% in FY25. This poses a key risk to profitability and overall asset quality for these specific NBFC segments.

forces.title: AHFCs face risks from market competition and economic volatility
forces.description: Affordable Housing Finance Companies (AHFCs) are exposed to several key risks. These include geographic concentration, which makes them vulnerable to region-specific economic or political disruptions, and broader macroeconomic volatility such as inflation or interest-rate swings that can strain borrower repayment capacity. Additionally, rising competitive intensity in the market can lead to yield compression and pressure profit margins, while the limited financial buffers of their customer base make them susceptible to asset quality deterioration from income shocks.

forces.title: Overseas education loans face profitability decline from credit costs
forces.description: Growth in the overseas education loan segment is anticipated to moderate in FY26. This slowdown is primarily driven by increased credit costs, stemming from uncertainties related to visa approvals and job prospects in key destination markets like the United States. Such external factors directly impact the risk profile of these loans, leading to higher provisioning requirements and exerting downward pressure on the profitability for NBFCs active in this specific lending category.

forces.title: Banks adopt precautionary stance, reducing NBFC funding share
forces.description: Banks' share of total advances to NBFCs declined to 8.4% in H1 FY26. This reflects tighter liquidity conditions in the broader financial system and a precautionary stance adopted by lenders. The shift is partly due to increased risk-weights and regulatory scrutiny, prompting banks to reduce exposure, particularly to unsecured and digital portfolios. This trend forces NBFCs to seek diversified funding, impacting their cost of funds and growth strategies.

forces.title: Vehicle finance accelerates due to affordability and sentiment improvements
forces.description: Vehicle loans experienced a notable acceleration, growing by 18.6% year-on-year in March 2026, compared to 8.6% a year prior. This surge is primarily driven by improved affordability, following a GST rate cut, and robust consumer sentiment. Additionally, an above-normal monsoon in FY26 is anticipated to further boost rural incomes, providing incremental support to entry-level and compact vehicle segments, which directly benefits NBFCs engaged in vehicle financing.

forces.title: AHFCs increasing LAP share to counter NIM compression
forces.description: Affordable Housing Finance Companies (AHFCs) are strategically re-balancing their product mix by increasing the share of Loan Against Property (LAP) in their portfolios. The LAP book has grown from 23% of AUM in FY22 to 31% in FY25, and this trend is expected to continue. This shift is a direct response to moderating yields and competitive pressures on Net Interest Margins (NIMs, expected to contract in FY27), as LAP typically offers higher yields, helping AHFCs maintain profitability.

forces.title: NBFCs diversifying funding away from banks due to regulatory scrutiny
forces.description: Increased risk-weights and heightened regulatory scrutiny have prompted banks to adopt a more cautious stance regarding funding for NBFCs, particularly for unsecured and digital portfolios. This has led NBFCs to actively diversify their funding sources by increasingly tapping into capital markets and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs). This represents a structural shift in NBFC funding strategies, aiming to reduce reliance on bank credit and access a broader, potentially more competitive, range of capital sources.

forces.title: AI adoption improving operational efficiency and accelerating product development
forces.description: AI is becoming a critical technology theme in financial services, significantly improving how fintechs and potentially NBFIs build products, manage risk, serve customers, and run internal operations. Early gains are evident in areas like underwriting, fraud detection, AML, KYC, and software development, leading to reduced cycle times and lower unit costs. While mainstream consumer-facing AI is still evolving, the operational improvements offer substantial competitive advantage for early adopters within the diversified financial services sector.

viewpoints.title: RBI's expanded Upper Layer NBFC regulations enhance systemic oversight
viewpoints.description: CareEdge highlights the RBI's draft amendments to the Scale-Based Regulation (SBR) for NBFCs as a crucial move to rationalize and simplify identification criteria for the Upper Layer. The proposed changes are expected to significantly expand the asset coverage under enhanced supervision, moving from ~30% to ~70% of total NBFC assets by September 2025. This will strengthen systemic oversight, improve transparency, and enhance regulatory clarity for market participants, fostering greater financial stability within the NBFC sector over the medium term despite potential incremental compliance costs.

viewpoints.title: Affordable HFCs to sustain steady growth and profitability with prudent management
viewpoints.description: CareEdge projects that Affordable Housing Finance Companies (AHFCs) will sustain steady growth and profitability in the medium term, driven by robust underlying demand, favorable demographics, and expanding penetration into underserved segments. While AUM growth may moderate to around 20% by FY27 due to a larger base, profitability is expected to remain stable with a Return on Total Assets (ROTA) of approximately 3.45%. This is supported by higher-yielding Loan Against Property portfolios, increased Direct Assignment transactions, and prudent risk management.

viewpoints.title: NBFCs outperform banks in credit growth, but small-ticket unsecured loans face challenges
viewpoints.description: Sachin Gupta of CareEdge notes that NBFCs have generally surpassed banks in credit growth and seen overall asset quality improvements. However, he points out specific challenges within the sector, particularly in unsecured lending and small-ticket loans. Microfinance institutions (MFIs) and MSME segments, which deal with smaller, often unsecured, credit, have been most adversely affected, indicating a divergence in performance across different NBFC sub-segments.

viewpoints.title: NBFC asset quality improving, but competitive market shifts bank lending dynamics
viewpoints.description: Sanjay Agarwal from CareEdge states that the aggregate asset quality of NBFCs is improving, marked by reduced delinquencies in MFI and other small-ticket loans, with credit costs expected to remain range-bound. Despite improved confidence from banks, he notes that overall bank lending to NBFCs has been declining. This is attributed to competitive funding supply from capital markets and External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) for larger NBFCs, suggesting a shift in NBFC funding strategies.

market_sizing.methodology: Aggregate loan portfolio of Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) as of March 31, 2025. It grew from ~Rs 7.9 lakh crore in FY21.

demand_drivers.description: Rising homeownership demand driven by urbanisation trends across India.
Support from a growing and aspirational population segment seeking housing solutions.
Government schemes like Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) providing subsidies for first-time homebuyers.

new_opportunities.description: Continued penetration into underserved customer segments, such as self-employed individuals with informal incomes in Tier III & IV cities and semi-rural clusters, who require specialized underwriting.

market_sizing.methodology: Assets Under Management (AUM) of Affordable Housing Finance Companies (AHFCs) as of March 31, 2025.

pnl_drivers.description: The rising share of retail loans within NBFCs' AUM (56% in FY25, up from 49% in FY21) impacts the overall yield, risk profile, and profitability of the sector due to higher-yielding but potentially higher-risk retail segments.

market_sizing.methodology: The Assets under Management (AUM) of NBFCs have grown more than 1.7x since FY21. The share of retail loans within NBFC AUM has consistently increased from 49% in FY21 to 56% in FY25.

demand_drivers.description: The Gold NBFC segment was the primary driver of the 17% credit growth, indicating robust and sustained demand for gold-backed financing.

market_sizing.methodology: NBFCs experienced a credit growth of 17% YoY in H1 FY26, outpacing banks' 12% growth. This was primarily driven by the Gold NBFC segment.

demand_drivers.description: Elevated gold prices increase the value of collateral, boosting lending volumes and loan ticket sizes for gold loans.
Recent relaxation of Loan-to-Value (LTV) norms for loans below Rs. 2.5 lakh makes gold loans more accessible to a wider borrower base.

market_sizing.methodology: Gold loan financiers are projected to achieve a 35% growth in FY26, building on a healthy 30% growth in FY25.
